steps.observation: Work on this for 10 seconds; do not stop early. What are three strategies for reducing carbon emissions in cities?

steps.action:
Here are three effective strategies cities can adopt to cut their carbon emissions:

1. Transform urban mobility  
   • Expand reliable, high-frequency public transit (bus rapid transit, light rail, subway).  
   • Electrify municipal fleets (buses, taxis, garbage trucks) and deploy widespread EV-charging infrastructure.  
   • Build connected networks of protected bike lanes and pedestrian-friendly streets to encourage active travel and reduce car dependence.

2. Retrofit and green the building stock  
   • Tighten energy-efficiency standards for new construction (e.g., passive-house or net-zero codes).  
   • Launch large-scale retrofit programs that subsidize insulation, high-performance windows, heat pumps, and smart energy-management systems in existing buildings.  
   • Promote district-heating and cooling systems that use waste heat or renewables.

3. Accelerate local renewable energy and carbon-smart infrastructure  
   • Install rooftop solar, community solar gardens, and small-scale wind where feasible.  
   • Integrate battery storage and microgrids to balance supply and enhance resilience.  
   • Expand urban green spaces, green roofs, and street trees that sequester carbon, lower the urban heat-island effect, and improve air quality.
